races.name: Behind The Lens Media Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: The Fixer
runners_data.note: Won over this C&D at Ffos Las in good style (1/5f/STA) but current form is worrying with four placed-or-worse runs since; genuine hold-up horse who needs pace to run into and will struggle if Call Time keeps sectionals moderate — 53 days off is also a concern.
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back gives The Fixer a recent form boost, though he was beaten into eighth last time out and hasn't run for 53 days; with a struggling yard sending him out at just 5% over the past fortnight, confidence in him resuming that winning thread is tempered.

runners_data.name: Little Jaybee
runners_data.note: David Evans runner who placed twice at Good on 5f course this season (3/5f/GOO, 3/5f/GOO) giving excellent specific course-and-going credentials; races from the rear but has shown more tactical flexibility than stablemates, and Joe Leavy's booking on a 16-day turnaround suggests stable confidence.
runners_data.comment: Little Jaybee shaped with promise on her two most recent starts, finishing third in each, and returns on a quick turnaround of just 16 days with experience of today's trip and going in her favour; yet to win in recent starts, but our rating of 71 marks her out as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Son Of Astar
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll sends this one with a good-ground second on the board (2/5f/SOF) and David Probert is a quality booking; natural hold-up operator whose true closer profile has been pushed into a mapped midfield position because the field cannot accommodate all hold-up types, temper expectations accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Son Of Astar shaped with promise when second three starts back, and he has run over today's trip and going, with our rating of 60 suggesting he holds strong claims against this field; the concern is a winless run of recent form and that 133 lb burden.

runners_data.name: Forever Glamorous
runners_data.note: Boasts a win and three places from six career starts including a Good-ground win over 5f, and the hood (headgear) could sharpen focus; her natural hold-up style is under pressure in this race shape as she is one of several genuine closers unable to get rearward berths, though her strong form figures on Good give her the best raw profile of the displaced hold-up group.
runners_data.comment: Forever Glamorous shaped with real promise when third last time out, and a winner two starts back, giving him a solid recent profile; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 133 lb from stall three is the weight to watch.

runners_data.name: Bridget's Baby
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago which is an obvious freshness concern, and a 5lb claimer (Myla Coppins) rides; showed a 1 and a 2 on Good in recent history so the going is fine, but being a true hold-up type mapped into midfield due to field compression makes her task harder than her decent form suggests.
runners_data.comment: Bridget's Baby won two starts back and was second three starts back, but a sixth last time out on just two days' rest leaves fitness a concern; she has run over today's trip and going before, though 131 lb is a stiff ask at this level.

runners_data.name: Call Time
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race and thus holds the structural key to this entire pace map; Good-ground record reads 0W1P from five runs and she has been absent 76 days, but the uncontested lead is a genuine tactical gift that makes raw OR 51 an unreliable guide to her chance today — headgear (p) worn previously.
runners_data.comment: Call Time has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 62 puts him among the chief dangers in this field, yet he arrives winless in his last five starts after a run of disappointing efforts, and 76 days off the track is the question his supporters must answer.

runners_data.name: Red Walls
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old whose recent form (88-380) is modest at best, and all five historical runs in the sample came over 6f which raises a legitimate distance concern dropping to 5f; a natural hold-up horse competing for rear positions in a crowded closer group, and the 18-day turnaround adds little to the case.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Red Walls faces a stiff task here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns in reasonable time, 18 days since his last outing.

runners_data.name: Kodi K
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a recent 2/5f/GOO on the board giving direct relevance to today's conditions; Liam Wright's 3lb claim helps the burden, but as another genuine hold-up type displaced into a mapped midfield role by field compression, his ability to get back and then generate late momentum on a modest pace is genuinely in doubt.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Kodi K faces a stiff task here, though he has run over today's distance and going before and the second two starts back at least shows he can threaten the places; drawn in stall one off 21 days, he needs more consistency.

races.paceDynamic: Call Time is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner sprint and, with no credible challenger for the lead, she can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without any pressure — a genuine lone-pace scenario over five furlongs at Ffos Las on Good ground. The absence of a pressing rival means the pace is unlikely to be searingly fast, which typically compresses sectionals and makes it harder for true hold-up horses to generate the momentum they need to reel in an uncontested leader. The field is, however, heavily populated with natural hold-up types — Forever Glamorous, Son Of Astar, Bridget's Baby, Red Walls, Kodi K and The Fixer are all genuine closers — meaning most of them will be competing for rear-to-midfield positions and will be denied their natural running style, with only a handful able to land a realistic tracking spot. This race shape strongly favours prominent or front-running profiles, and among the hold-up pack, those with the strongest Good-ground form and the tactical flexibility to sit slightly closer than usual will carry an obvious advantage; pure hold-up specialists operating at the back of a slowly-run 5f field face the steepest ask.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Call Time Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Call Time jumps cleanly and controls an honest but uncontested tempo throughout the five furlongs.
scenarios.body: Call Time sets her own rhythm from the front with no rival willing or able to press her, arriving at the final furlong with a significant energy advantage over the pack behind; at OR 51 she is the lowest-rated runner but the race shape hands her a structural edge that raw ratings cannot fully capture.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a runner tracks Call Time in second or third at a safe distance and produces a clean late surge to collar her inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting just off the lead avoids the worst of the bunched hold-up traffic and arrives fresh enough to challenge as Call Time's advantage narrows; this rewards those with the tactical intelligence and jockey craft to find a position against their natural inclination.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If Call Time goes off too fast in isolation and ties up in the final 100 yards, allowing the massed hold-up group to arrive in a wave.
scenarios.body: The compressed group of hold-up horses, all running closer than ideal, would need the front end to visibly stop to generate the ground they require; given the one-pace scenario, this is a low-probability event but cannot be dismissed entirely on Good turf.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Draw And Position Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If the field fans wide from the outset and the race breaks into isolated pockets with no coherent pace structure.
scenarios.body: Multiple hold-up runners unable to secure their preferred position create positional chaos that hands an advantage to whichever runner finds the cleanest run and widest berth; this scenario is particularly speculative given the redistribution pressure in this field.

watchPoints.text: Call Time's start is critical — if Taylor Fisher gets her away cleanly and to the front unchallenged inside the first furlong, the entire race shape is set in stone with every other runner chasing from the rear.

With six horses of genuine hold-up style all competing for rear-to-midfield ground, watch for significant early positional shuffling and potential interference in the first two furlongs as none can all get their preferred position.

Forever Glamorous, Bridget's Baby and Son Of Astar are the three redistributed hold-up types with the strongest recent Good-ground form credentials — if any of them manages to break quickly and secure an unplanned prominent berth, their profile improves dramatically and they become live dangers.

Little Jaybee's two recent placed efforts over this exact 5f trip on Good ground for David Evans make her course-and-going profile stand out from the rest of the hold-up group — watch whether Joe Leavy attempts to ride her slightly closer than usual given the race shape.

Red Walls dropping from 6f to 5f is worth monitoring in the market — if support comes for her despite the trip concern, it may signal handler confidence in a fitness or handicap angle that the form book does not fully reflect.

races.name: Golwg Gwendraeth Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Bella Bisbee
runners_data.note: Five-year-old mare who races prominently and has placed form on good ground at this trip; Scott Dixon's yard is in modest 14-day form (1/25) but she brings solid course-and-distance profile and a clean draw at 7½f on turf makes her well placed to slot in second or third off the leader early.|
runners_data.comment: Bella Bisbee shaped well when third last time out and a winner six starts back, and she brings experience of today's trip and going into this; the worry is a trainer firing at just 5% in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Lerwick
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer who is best fresh and drops back in trip having run over 8-10f recently; the headgear note (best) is worth checking and Callum Hutchinson keeps it simple, but 24 days off and a likely wide draw mean he needs the race to be genuinely run to produce his finish.|
runners_data.comment: Lerwick comes here off a win last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a serious contender, and our rating marks him as the top-ranked runner in the field; the main risk is that his four starts before that victory brought modest efforts, hinting at some inconsistency.

runners_data.name: The Stone Power
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett three-year-old who bounced back to winning form last time over 8f on good ground and races prominently; Rhys Clutterbuck takes over and the top-weight burden at 135lbs is the key query, though a yard in strong 14-day form (3/31) suggests confidence.|
runners_data.comment: The Stone Power won last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, making him a clear threat from stall two carrying 135 lb; the solitary pull-up in recent starts is the one blot punters will need to forgive.

runners_data.name: Santiago Boy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who carries the hood (b) and has consistent placed form at 7-8f on varying ground; Harry Vigors' 5lb claim helps offset the burden and 9 days between runs is a quick turnaround, but he must avoid being squeezed out during the early prominent scramble that this race shape creates.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent sort who has finished second in each of his last two starts and returns on a quick nine-day turnaround in good heart, having run over today's distance and going before; winless in recent starts but his profile fits these conditions well enough to make him our pick from stall one carrying 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Mountain Of Light
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old with just three runs who placed second at 8f on good ground last time; Stevie Donohoe partners and the horse wants to be prominent, but the very thin race record makes him difficult to fully assess and he may lack the experience to navigate a bustling early position.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, with an eighth and seventh bracketing a runner-up finish, Mountain Of Light looks up against it from stall ten carrying 130 lb, and our rating of 69 ranks her ninth of ten; experience over today's trip and going at least counts for something.

runners_data.name: Dappled Light
runners_data.note: In fine form having won three of his last five at 8f on good ground, but his natural desire to race prominently cannot be accommodated cleanly in this field — he is likely to find himself squeezed into a midfield berth he doesn't want; with a STYLE_FIT of 0.92 and 43 days off, his chance is tempered by circumstance despite excellent recent form.|
runners_data.comment: Dappled Light won back-to-back before consecutive runner-up efforts, showing consistency in recent starts, though 43 days off the track is a fitness question mark; he has distance and going experience to call on, but 130 lb is a testing burden from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Gelato
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type who won last time at 8f on soft for Adrian Wintle, but the yard has had no winners in 14 days and the apprentice rider Taryn Langley (5lb claim) is navigating a hold-up role in a field where the pace may not be strong enough to create the gap she needs late.|
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back but has been below par either side of that success, finishing fifth last time out and well beaten in three of her last five; Gelato has run over today's trip and going, carries 126 lb from stall four, and returns after 24 days off.

runners_data.name: Cypriot Diaspora
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race, giving him a significant positional advantage; Ryan Kavanagh's 3lb claim keeps the weight manageable and recent placed form at 8f on good ground confirms he handles the conditions, though dropping to 7½f on a flat track where he can dictate without pressure is the key tactical asset.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Cypriot Diaspora faces a stiff ask ranked eighth of ten on our figures, though she has run over today's distance and going before and a return to form two starts back — when second — offers a slender foothold seven days on.

runners_data.name: Nebbia
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer stepping up slightly in trip from recent 5-6f runs on good ground; David Probert is a quality booking but the horse needs a genuinely fast-run race to generate the finish, and with just one hold-up specialist ahead of him in the queue, clean late running is far from guaranteed.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Nebbia does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a return from 42 days off could freshen her up, though that eighth last time out is hard to ignore against this level of opposition.

runners_data.name: Grimese's Special
runners_data.note: Long-absent (80 days) three-year-old with the blinkers on, whose natural style is hold-up but who may find herself pushed further back than even that in a field with limited true pace; the redistribution out of her natural mapping position underlines that she needs things to fall perfectly, and a 7lb claimer in Isobelle Chalmers adds inexperience into the equation.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Grimese's Special faces a stiff task after 80 days off the track and a run of three poor efforts in her last three starts, though she has distance and going experience to call on and showed she can win in recent form.

races.paceDynamic: Cypriot Diaspora is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only one horse naturally wanting to lead, is likely to control proceedings from the front at a sustainable gallop on good ground over 7½ furlongs at Ffos Las — a track that suits prominent, rail-hugging runners. Behind him, Bella Bisbee, The Stone Power, Santiago Boy, and Mountain Of Light all want to race prominently, creating genuine scrimmaging for the first two or three positions between the two-furlong and one-furlong pole as rivals make their challenges. This field holds more prominent-type runners than can all get their natural position: Bella Bisbee and The Stone Power are the likeliest to actually secure that front-rank berth behind Cypriot Diaspora, with Santiago Boy and Mountain Of Light likely squeezed wider or slightly further back than ideal. A controlled, honest pace set by a sole front-runner who is not pressured into overdoing it is the dominant shape here, and this race shape most clearly favours prominent horses who can slot in cleanly behind the leader and pounce in the straight without having to fight for position early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Cypriot Diaspora leads unchallenged at a fair but uncontested pace and the prominent runners slot cleanly behind him.
scenarios.body: Cypriot Diaspora dictates a measured tempo and the prominent types immediately behind him save ground and energy, putting them in the ideal position to sweep past from 2f out on the home turn; the rail-friendly track at Ffos Las rewards those who travel kindly close to the pace without burning petrol early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Holds On, Fade Denied
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow and Cypriot Diaspora slows the race to a crawl, making his stamina advantage decisive.
scenarios.body: A near-walk early turns the race into a sprint from 2f out, which suits the leader who dictates and then quickens on his own terms, with those who pressed him unable to go past and hold-up runners left with too much ground to make up; Cypriot Diaspora's recent placed form on good ground and step back to a manageable trip makes this credible.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent battle for position causes enough early pressure to string the field out and create a truly run race that plays into late finishers' hands.
scenarios.body: Lerwick, Nebbia, and Gelato would need the prominent traffic to knock each other out of contention in the straight to leave a gap, and a stronger-than-expected pace would allow them to reel in tired rivals from 2f out; this scenario is partially discounted because Grimese's Special and Dappled Light — both redistibuted out-of-role runners — are not genuine closers in this configuration.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scenario, Traffic Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent types collide for position between 2f and 1f out, causing interference and opening the race up to any survivor.
scenarios.body: A scrappy mid-race scramble would produce an unpredictable finish where the horse who avoids trouble and finds clear running at the right moment wins regardless of style; the redistributed runners Dappled Light and Grimese's Special are least likely to benefit given they are already racing out of their natural role and need a clear passage that this chaotic shape rarely provides.

watchPoints.text: Bella Bisbee, The Stone Power, Santiago Boy, and Mountain Of Light are all competing for the same two prominent slots behind Cypriot Diaspora — watch the opening two furlongs for bumping, crowding, or one of these runners being completely knocked out of their stride before the race settles.

Cypriot Diaspora leads alone and unenforced but his form figures (986324) show he has faded repeatedly in recent races — if he strings them out on the home turn without a strong pace behind him, the fade point between 2f and 1f out is the critical watch moment.

Dappled Light is racing out of role having been mapped to midfield despite being a natural prominent type; if he tries to force his way forward from a wider draw, he risks burning energy and compromising both his own run and those of the genuine hold-up horses immediately around him.

Grimese's Special returns after 80 days off with blinkers applied — watch the paddock and early running for any signs of freshness or greenness that could cause interference towards the rear of the field where the hold-up runners are clustered.

Lerwick has a "best" headgear note suggesting a specific gear requirement — confirm pre-race whether this is applied today, as its absence would meaningfully alter the case for this hold-up performer producing a late run.

races.name: Dandara Homes Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Esplanade
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly trained by Charles Hills, carrying a lofty OR of 120 but her form figures of 0 and 6 suggest she has not come close to that mark in either start; Harry Vigors (5lb claim) rides and her one similar-going outing produced a midfield finish, making her a speculative closer who needs the pace to collapse.|

runners_data.name: Graniteville
runners_data.note: Marco Botti's hold-up type has four runs under her belt and recorded a placed finish on Good going, but her form string of 0-464 reads as consistently mid-pack without threatening; Benoit de la Sayette takes the ride and the 9-day turnaround is noted, though she will need a stronger gallop than Withtearsinmyeyes is likely to set to exploit her closing style.|

runners_data.name: Sydney Rock
runners_data.note: Oliver Cole's filly has placed three times from recent starts and holds genuine hold-up tendencies — she is displayed at midfield on the pace map purely because the field has more rear-of-field types than positions allow, and her actual racing position will be closer to last; a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.92 confirms she is racing out of role in this shape, which should temper confidence in any scenario requiring her to race forward.|

runners_data.name: Withtearsinmyeyes
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's consistent front runner has four consecutive placed finishes on Good or Tapeta, two of them at this distance, and David Probert's experience is a significant asset in controlling the tempo from the front in a small field; she is the only confirmed pace-setter and faces zero pressure for the lead, making her the pivotal horse around which this entire race is shaped.|

runners_data.name: Zupa Trupa
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's filly returns after 261 days off the track with only a single fourth-place run at 7f on Tapeta to her name, so her style and distance aptitude at a mile on turf remain genuinely unknown; the yard has placed three winners from 31 runners over the past 14 days, and an unknown ceiling in a small field means she cannot be dismissed entirely, but the lengthy absence demands caution.|

races.paceDynamic: Withtearsinmyeyes is the lone confirmed front runner in a five-runner field and, with no rival likely to dispute the lead seriously, David Probert can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this flat Ffos Las mile on Good ground. The hold-up runners — Esplanade, Graniteville and Sydney Rock — will be tracking from the rear, meaning the pace is set entirely by one horse and the tempo is unlikely to be strong enough to burn Withtearsinmyeyes off. Zupa Trupa is unknown in terms of style after a single run and may slot in behind the leader by default, providing no material challenge to Withtearsinmyeyes's control. This shape squarely favours a front runner who can dictate and quicken, or a genuinely progressive closer with the engine to bridge a steady-pace gap late — late-closers face the toughest task when the leader controls the fractions unchallenged. Note that the field contains more hold-up types than the pace map can place at the rear; Sydney Rock is a genuine hold-up horse shown in midfield on the map, but its true position is likely to be at the back, meaning its chance in any scenario requiring midfield positioning should be discounted accordingly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Controls, Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Withtearsinmyeyes gets an uncontested lead and sets a measured, comfortable gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Probert settles Withtearsinmyeyes in front, controls the fractions on this flat mile, and has enough in reserve to repel late challengers from the rear; with a small field and no pace rival, the leader's energy expenditure is minimal. Front-running hold-up horses with consistent placed form and a good record on Good ground thrive in this shape, and Withtearsinmyeyes's four consecutive placed runs reinforce its suitability.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Closer Reels In
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and the hold-up horses conserve enough energy to mount a sustained challenge in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A crawl in the early stages compresses the field and turns the race into a sprint finish, giving Esplanade or Graniteville a chance to close from off the pace with a powerful late burst. Esplanade carries the highest OR in the field and, if producing anything close to that rating, possesses the class to reel in a front runner who has gone too slowly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutant Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Zupa Trupa, lightly raced after 261 days off, shows significantly improved form and slot in prominently to challenge.
scenarios.body: Ralph Beckett's lightly raced filly has shown enough in a single start to suggest there is untapped ability, and a long absence followed by a yard strike rate of 3/31 over 14 days keeps expectations measured but the upside is real. If Zupa Trupa travels prominently behind the leader and produces a forward move into the straight, the unknown ceiling becomes a major asset.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Muddle, Closers Foiled
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace leaves hold-up types with too much ground to make up in the straight and the race is run too slowly for them to close.
scenarios.body: Sydney Rock and Graniteville, operating from the rear in a small, slowly run field, find themselves with no cover and insufficient pace to chase into, leaving their finishing kicks ineffective. In this shape the winner comes from the front or the handy position, reinforcing the leader's advantage even further.

watchPoints.text: Withtearsinmyeyes — if Probert establishes a comfortable uncontested lead within the first furlong, the race is essentially his to control; watch whether any rival attempts to close the gap early on the first bend, as that would be the only credible threat to his front-running advantage.

Zupa Trupa — a 261-day absence and a single run on a completely different surface make her behaviour in the early stages entirely unpredictable; if Rhys Clutterbuck chooses to press Withtearsinmyeyes for the lead rather than settle, the pace dynamic changes meaningfully.

Esplanade — her OR of 120 is dramatically detached from her actual form figures of 0 and 6, and if there is any substance behind that rating she is the most dangerous late mover, but the market will reveal whether connections or the assessor have the better read on her ability.

Sydney Rock — genuine hold-up style means she is likely to race last of five regardless of the map position shown; in a slowly run race over a mile, the ground she needs to make up in the straight may simply be too great for a horse with no wins from eight starts.

races.name: Thomas Arms Llanelli Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Belltony
runners_data.note: Poor recent form (74655) with no wins or places on good, and 59 days off; a genuine deep hold-up horse whose redistribution to midfield on the map actually flatters its likely race position — expect it near last and needing more than this pace shape offers.
runners_data.comment: Belltony catches the eye as the top-rated runner in this field, and he has experience of both today's trip and conditions; the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts and returns after 59 days off.

runners_data.name: Dinah Myte
runners_data.note: John Gallagher's yard is 1/7 in the last 14 days, and Dinah Myte showed a win at 8f on standard and placed twice on good at 10f — the trip back to a mile suits, but its natural back-of-the-field instinct will make securing a prominent slot difficult in a field this congested.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last on our figures and carrying a hefty 135 lb, Dinah Myte faces a stiff task, and a sixth-place finish last time out does little to inspire confidence, though she has run over today's trip and going before and does own a win in her last six starts.

runners_data.name: Eye Of The Water
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here and the key pace-shape horse; 10-year-old veteran with headgear (p), has placed at 8f on good, and Callum Hutchinson will be able to dictate every fraction — the concern is whether it has the finishing kick to hold off a chasing pack at the distance.
runners_data.comment: Eye Of The Water has shown a knack for hitting the frame, finishing third two of his last three outings, and he has experience over today's trip and conditions — yet to score in recent starts, and 58 days off the track is the question he must answer here.

runners_data.name: King Of The Dance
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with the highest sim-going strike rate (8/15) in the field, placed three times on good at 8f, and only 7 days since last run — blinkered and ridden by a 7lb claimer which is a slight concern, but this is the profile best suited to tracking the pace and pouncing.
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back and runner-up five starts back, King Of The Dance brings solid recent placing form into this, and at just seven days since his last start he arrives fit and ready; has run over today's trip and going, and 135 lb from stall five is a workable enough ask for a gelding yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Launceston
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's yard has been busy (3/36 in 14 days), but Launceston's form reads as a chronic non-stayer at longer trips and a modest performer at a mile — the horse's true hold-up style, pushed into midfield by the crowded rear, means it will struggle to find a winning position from where it will actually race.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Launceston faces a stiff task ranked eighth of ten on our figures, and a 46-day absence adds to the concern; he has run over today's trip and going, and a career-best effort in recent starts would be needed.

runners_data.name: Pebble Dash
runners_data.note: Form figure of 3 last time (8f/standard) is its best recent effort, but prior to that a string of fourths and worse; David Probert is an upgrade in the saddle, yet this horse's natural hold-up style will keep it in a portion of the field where Eye Of The Water's steady pace offers little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Pebble Dash is hard to fancy, though he does return after 34 days and has run over today's trip and going before; a third last time out at least suggests he retains some ability.

runners_data.name: Private Officer
runners_data.note: The 303-day absence is a glaring concern — last ran in August last year — and the form string (719/0-) is poor; the one win on good at 8f is the solitary positive, but asking a hold-up horse to return to winning ways after nearly a year off in a competitive field requires significant blind faith.
runners_data.comment: Private Officer showed a winning turn of foot when landing the spoils three starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going is a clear asset carrying 135 lb from stall 2; the main concern is a lengthy 303-day absence.

runners_data.name: West Hill Rosie
runners_data.note: Jeff Mullins runner with 0 wins from 5 on good going in its last six starts, all at 10f — this mile trip is shorter than recent assignments, which could help, but the 0W/1P record on similar ground and no headgear change means it offers little pace-shape advantage.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, West Hill Rosie does have experience over today's trip and shaped with some promise when third two starts back, though a sixth last time out suggests she faces a stiff task from stall six carrying 135 lb off an official mark of 50.

runners_data.name: Alice's Influence
runners_data.note: David Evans' three-year-old is the most consistent horse in the field with a 1W/4P record on good going (6/11 sim-going) and a 6lbs weight advantage over older rivals; visored, recently active (16 days), and likely to push forward from a natural hold-up base — the profile that best combines consistency, form, and weight.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in her last six starts, Alice's Influence does bring distance and going experience to the table, and 16 days since her last run suggests she arrives fresh; third and second efforts in recent starts hint at ability, though a career-best finish remains elusive.

runners_data.name: Castlekeely
runners_data.note: James Owen's yard leads all trainers here at 5/46 in 14 days, and the 2nd at 8f on good last time stands out as a strong recent effort; the three-year-old's 6lb weight advantage is valuable, and while its redistribution to midfield masks a tendency to race prominently, it is among the most likely to actually secure that forward position on race day.
runners_data.comment: Castlekeely showed his best recent form when second last time out, and has run over today's trip and going before, but he carries 129 lb from stall nine and has been winless in his last five starts, leaving him with plenty to prove against stronger company.

races.paceDynamic: Eye Of The Water is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to push it, will control this mile contest from the outset at Ffos Las on good ground, setting a measured, sustainable tempo that is unlikely to be contested. Behind it, the pack is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types — King Of The Dance, West Hill Rosie, Private Officer, Alice's Influence, Castlekeely, Dinah Myte, Belltony, Launceston, and Pebble Dash all have hold-up or midfield tendencies, meaning the field will bunch up in Eye Of The Water's wake rather than stretch into a true test of stamina. This shape — a lone leader at a controlled pace with a wall of closers unable to split into natural positions — classically favours the horse on the front end who controls the fractions and a runner with enough tactical versatility to sit just off the pace and produce a decisive burst in the straight. The field holds considerably more genuine hold-up horses than the race can accommodate at the rear: Alice's Influence, Castlekeely, and Dinah Myte are the most likely to push forward from their natural roles and secure a prominent position, given their OR, recent runs, and jockey profile, while true backmarkers like Belltony, Launceston, and Pebble Dash will be forced to race closer than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Eye Of The Water dictates an unchallenged, steady gallop and the hold-up pack cannot organise a meaningful challenge in time.
scenarios.body: Eye Of The Water slips the field around the final turn, building a lead the closers cannot close down on the flat good surface; this scenario rewards whoever can travel prominently just behind and pounce, rather than those coming from deep.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Upsetters Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Alice's Influence or Castlekeely, pushing forward from their natural hold-up roles, secure a prominent pitch and unleash a sustained run from two out.
scenarios.body: Travelling in second or third, a horse like Alice's Influence (consistent top-three form at 8f on good, weight advantage at 129lbs) or Castlekeely hits the front early in the straight before Eye Of The Water can respond; the steady pace suits these lightly-weighted three-year-olds who can quicken off it.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough mid-race to string out the field and leave late runners with ground to make up on tiring horses.
scenarios.body: A faster early tempo — unlikely but possible if Castlekeely or Dinah Myte push forward aggressively — could create a truly run race where King Of The Dance or West Hill Rosie, picking their way through, arrive with a late rattle; however, this scenario is discounted because the surplus of hold-up types means few will truly be at the back to benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaotic Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the slow early tempo produces a sprint finish with the entire field arriving together and race-day luck in running becoming the decisive factor.
scenarios.body: Eye Of The Water's lead evaporates as jockeys throw caution aside entering the straight, turning the race into a cavalry charge where positional luck, draw, and a clear run matter most; Private Officer's one win came at 8f on good and could theoretically benefit from chaos, but his 303-day absence makes this speculative.

watchPoints.text: Eye Of The Water (front-runner) controls the pace entirely — watch whether Callum Hutchinson increases tempo at the 3f pole to deny the closers a clean run, which would transform this from an easy lead into a decisive breakaway.

Alice's Influence and Castlekeely, both natural hold-up horses, are likely to compete for the same prominent position in the first furlong — if both push forward aggressively, they could disrupt each other's rhythm and hand Eye Of The Water an even more uncontested lead.

King Of The Dance runs only 7 days after its last race with a 7lb claimer in the saddle (Donagh Murphy) — monitor pre-race market moves, as a well-backed favourite ridden by a claimer off a quick turnaround in a pace-shape race is a significant betting signal.

Private Officer's 303-day layoff means its fitness is entirely unverifiable from its form string — any significant market support for this horse in the ring would be a strong trainer confidence signal worth tracking.

The clustering of hold-up types in the back half means late-race traffic is almost inevitable — horses drawn widest (check final draw) may have a cleaner passage in the straight than those trapped on the rail behind a wall of hold-up rivals.

races.name: K P Tyres Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Seraglio Point
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Hughie Morrison and David Probert who has run in heavy going and shown ability on good ground (2 placed in 4 sim-going runs), but has a patchy recent form string of 6-8-3-0 and faces a stiff test running against two other genuine pace horses who will challenge for the lead.|
runners_data.comment: Seraglio Point shaped with promise when third two starts back, has run over today's trip and going, and his rating of 67 ranks him second in this field — the risk is that he has been winless in recent starts and must bounce back from an unplaced effort last time.

runners_data.name: Sunshine And Roses
runners_data.note: Rose Dawes (5) rides for Jack Channon; this hold-up filly has strong recent placed form including a win and two runner-up finishes in her last five, three of which came on soft/standard going, and her 10-day turnaround suggests she is in a rich vein — stamina for 1m2f is the key question after running mainly at 8f.|
runners_data.comment: Sunshine And Roses arrives in fine fettle just ten days since her last start, boasting a second last time out and a win three starts back, and she has experience over today's trip and conditions; the main risk is whether 135 lb from stall 11 blunts her finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Katalyst
runners_data.note: Ryan Kavanagh (3) partners this hold-up type for Muir & Grassick who are firing at a 17% strike rate over 14 days; blinkers are applied, trip looks suitable after placed efforts at 9f-10f on good ground, and five good-ground runs in recent history suggest the going is no concern — the congested rear of the field is the tactical threat.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Katalyst does at least step back up having finished second three starts back, and she has run over today's trip and going before; a seventh last time out, however, means she must bounce back sharply from stall seven carrying 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Beryl's Girl
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's three-year-old wears a hood and races prominently, with a win at 10f on good ground 23 days ago giving her strong course-trip-going credentials; Callum Hutchinson takes over in the saddle and the hat-trick bid will be harder against this competitive field, but her position just off the warring front-runners gives her a natural tactical advantage.|
runners_data.comment: Beryl's Girl won three starts back but has posted a seventh and a fourth since, and with her trainer in poor recent form — just one winner from 29 runners in the last fortnight — confidence is limited, even if she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Grindleton
runners_data.note: Ebrahim Nader partners this Kubler-trained front-runner who has placed at 10f and 12f on good and soft — the stamina is proven and the step to 10f fits; but being one of three confirmed pace horses means he faces a genuine battle for the lead from flag-fall, and his trainer's 0-from-10 over 14 days is worth noting.|
runners_data.comment: Grindleton arrives here in fine fettle just 24 days after finishing second last time out, and was second three starts back too, giving him strong claims as the top-rated runner in the field; he has experience over today's trip and going, though a win has so far eluded him in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Lc Tiffen
runners_data.note: Lisa Williamson, on a hot 14-day strike rate of 1/3, sends out this filly whose most recent run was a win at 10f on good ground — the form and trip fit well; she is a genuine hold-up runner at heart, and with multiple similar types in the field she is likely to find herself further forward than ideal, which will test her ability to settle and produce her usual late run.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom two on our figures and carrying 132 lb from stall eight, Lc Tiffen is hard to fancy despite her win last time out; she has experience of today's distance and going, but her inconsistent recent record leaves her tough to trust.

runners_data.name: Thai Princess
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle's mare is tackling 1m2f for the first time having run exclusively at 6f-8f; her best sim-going return was a third on firm which is faster than today's good going, and while the step up in trip could unlock more, the stamina question is very real and Finley Marsh will need to ride her cold off the hot pace to give her any chance.|
runners_data.comment: Thai Princess arrives here 44 days fresher, has run over today's trip, and our rating of 62 puts her firmly in contention from stall 3, with that third last time out the most encouraging recent signal — the risk is she remains winless in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Pangbourne
runners_data.note: Roger Teal's yard has been in excellent form over 14 days (3/12); this is a genuine hold-up runner who has placed twice from the rear at 1m and 1m2f on standard and soft going — good ground is unproven — and with three other hold-up types also in the field, Owen Lewis (5) may struggle to get the relaxed ride that brings out the best in him.|
runners_data.comment: Pangbourne has shown consistency without a win in recent starts, her two runner-up efforts offset by a string of fifths, and 14 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh; experience over today's trip helps, but an official mark of 56 and ranking eighth of eleven point to a midfield ceiling.

runners_data.name: Give Me Sun
runners_data.note: Benoit de la Sayette rides for Patrick Owens; this confirmed front-runner has a win and three places from five good-ground starts including a win over 10f, making him arguably the most accomplished of the three pace horses — if either of the others blinks first in the early exchanges, Give Me Sun is best equipped to control proceedings from the front.|
runners_data.comment: Winner last time out and placed twice in her last five starts, Give Me Sun arrives with solid recent form, though her official rating of 56 and a tough 131 lb burden may test her resolve; she has run over today's trip and going before and draws stall five.

runners_data.name: Ivat Ghia
runners_data.note: Mark Usher's gelding (same trainer as Summer Oasis) wears a hood and has placed twice at 8f on good ground; a natural hold-up type who will find his path to the rear partially blocked in this field-shape, and the step from 8f to 10f is an unknown quantity — Tyler Heard will need to find a clean passage if the late run is to materialise.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with two successive runner-up finishes offering some consolation, Ivat Ghia nevertheless ranks ninth of eleven on our figures and faces a stiff ask from stall nine carrying 126 lb, making her hard to fancy despite the going experience.

runners_data.name: Summer Oasis
runners_data.note: ⚠ Flagged as one who fades in the finish; Harry Vigors (5) partners this Mark Usher runner who has recorded no finishes better than sixth in the last five runs and has been beaten into rear positions on soft, standard, and stamina tracks — the significant drop in OR to 47 and the redistribution into midfield from a natural hold-up position compounds the concern here.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of this field on our figures, Summer Oasis faces a stiff ask, though 36 days since her last run leaves her fresh and stall four is a neutral enough pitch from which to try to reverse a run of poor form.

races.paceDynamic: Seraglio Point, Grindleton, and Give Me Sun are all confirmed front-runners in a field of 11, guaranteeing a strong, contested gallop from the outset over 1m2f on good ground at Ffos Las — a combination that will thoroughly test stamina and punish horses that burn energy early fighting for position. These three will likely jostle for supremacy down the back straight, setting a pace that compresses the field and leaves little margin for error at the business end. The sustained gallop they create strongly favours hold-up horses and genuine stayers who can absorb the pace and deliver a sustained late run, rather than those who need to make their effort from the front. However, Lc Tiffen, Pangbourne, and Ivat Ghia — all natural hold-up types — have been redistributed into midfield on the map because the field contains more hold-up runners than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; in practice, Give Me Sun or Grindleton are most likely to secure the prominent roles alongside Seraglio Point, with the true hold-up brigade unable to get as far back as they would ideally want.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War Burns Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners cut each other's throats and the gallop is genuinely punishing throughout, setting up a race for the strongest stayer.
scenarios.body: Seraglio Point, Grindleton, and Give Me Sun will fight for supremacy and the tempo will be relentlessly high, leaving them vulnerable in the final two furlongs as stamina drains; horses that have been tracking just off the pace or conserving energy from midfield will sweep past the dying leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three pace-setters asserts early and the others cede ground, allowing a solo leader to establish a comfortable rhythm rather than a true war.
scenarios.body: A controlled lead at a fair but not brutal gallop is far kinder to the front-runner, giving them a chance to dictate and sprint clear before the hold-up horses can wind up their challenge from behind; Give Me Sun, who has won and placed from front-running positions at 10f on good ground, is best suited to converting this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace war is so extreme that it creates a truly truly true closers' race and the hold-up runners — despite redistribution — manage to settle far enough back to launch a telling late run.
scenarios.body: Sunshine And Roses and Katalyst, both genuine hold-up performers with recent placed form at this trip or shorter on good ground, are best placed to benefit if the carnage at the front is complete; the caveat is that the several redistributed midfield types mean the back of the field may be more congested than ideal, blunting the late charge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the early scramble for position briefly intense but settles, allowing a horse tracking just off the leaders in third or fourth to quicken neatly when the front rank tires.
scenarios.body: Beryl's Girl, who won at 10f on good ground with a prominent style and wears a hood to aid concentration, is ideally positioned to benefit from this shape — close enough to the action without burning fuel in the early war; Thai Princess, stepping sharply up in trip, is the outsider who could outrun her odds if she settles beautifully off the pace.

watchPoints.text: Seraglio Point, Grindleton, and Give Me Sun are all drawn to lead and will likely clash hard in the first half-mile — watch for one or more capitulating suddenly in the final two furlongs as the price of the early battle is paid.

Lc Tiffen, Pangbourne, and Ivat Ghia are genuine hold-up horses who may find themselves unable to secure their preferred position at the rear with so many similar types in the field — watch for crowding and lost ground in the early stages.

Beryl's Girl is attempting to follow up a recent win and switches jockey to Callum Hutchinson — watch whether she can settle cleanly in her prominent role without being dragged into the early pace battle.
Thai Princess faces the stiffest stamina test of her career stepping from 8f to 10f — watch her travelling in the final three furlongs to judge whether the extra distance is within her range.

Summer Oasis has a flagged tendency to fade in the finish and is running from a natural hold-up position that the race shape will not accommodate — watch for early signs of her being shuffled wide or outpaced as the pace war unfolds ahead of her.

races.name: Noah's Ark Christmas Party Race Day Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Hibernate
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner here, Ed Dunlop's four-year-old won over 12f on Firm and again on Good last time, and Mason Paetel's 3lb claim is a useful asset; uncontested lead over this trip on Good ground is his optimum scenario, though his OR=70 rating means rivals arrive in handicap range.
runners_data.comment: Ran to a second two starts back and has winning form in recent starts, so the ability is there, but a fourth last time out and a 37-day absence leave questions; has run over today's trip and going, and 135 lb is no featherweight at a rating of 70.

runners_data.name: Crackergee
runners_data.note: Hughie Morrison's hold-up performer has a sole win on Soft over 12f, and his Flat-handicap form on standard going is thin — 0W0P from 13 similar-going runs paints a stark picture; David Probert keeps the ride but this course and conditions profile is short on confidence.
runners_data.comment: Crackergee landed a win two starts back and has run over today's trip, giving him a solid platform to threaten here off a mark of 70, though that fifth last time out after a 46-day absence raises a question over his sharpness returning to action.

runners_data.name: Robusto
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's six-year-old carries a hood and is in career form having won over 12f on Good last time at OR=69; Harry Vigors's 5lb claim helps his weight, and his prominent racing style positions him ideally to stalk Hibernate and challenge in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Robusto won last time out and was third two starts back, giving him strong recent form credentials, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; a struggling trainer yard is the one reservation, but his profile marks him out as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Raintown
runners_data.note: Progressive six-year-old fitted with a pacing hood, recently winning over 10f on Good and placing multiple times at similar conditions (5/15 runs, 1W4P); a hold-up type by style but compact recent form over shorter trips suggests fitness is there — the extra 4f is the question mark.
runners_data.comment: Raintown arrives in solid nick, second last time out and a winner two starts back, with experience over today's trip and going and a lively rating to support his claims; the chief concern is whether 133 lb blunts his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Flightofthephoenix
runners_data.note: Charles Hills's four-year-old won over 11f on Standard and ran second over 10f on Good, showing the form is genuine — but his natural profile is a true hold-up type pushed into a midfield map slot here because of traffic, and the style-fit flag tempers confidence in him getting a clean run from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Flightofthephoenix won last time out and was second two starts back, but her two seventh-placed efforts three and four starts ago temper expectations; she has going experience to call on and arrives fresh enough at 18 days, though 133 lb is a significant weight to shoulder.

runners_data.name: King's Castle
runners_data.note: David Simcock's nine-year-old is arguably the course and distance specialist in this field with nine similar-going runs, four wins, and eight places — Taryn Langley (5lb claim) takes the ride, and his prominent style means he is beautifully positioned to capitalise if Hibernate weakens late.
runners_data.comment: Consistently in the mix — King's Castle has finished third or better in three of his last five starts and returns here in good order after 22 days, with experience of today's trip and conditions; the concern is he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Luan
runners_data.note: Nick Scholfield's four-year-old carries a tongue-tie and has winning form on Standard ground over 12f, but his sole Good-going start produced a 13th — he is a genuine hold-up type forced further forward on the map, and the style mismatch plus modest Good-ground data significantly limits expectation.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in his last five starts show Luan has ability on a good day, and he has run over today's trip before, but finishing ninth last time out and ranking last on our figures makes him very hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: Shaffron
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's four-year-old returns from 106 days off — the longest layoff in the field — and arrives with 0W1P from seven similar-going starts; a natural closer whose best form is elusive on turf, the combination of the absence, redistribution to midfield, and low strike-rate in this going profile makes him a difficult proposition.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and absent for 106 days, Shaffron is hard to fancy from seventh in the rankings, though she has run over today's distance and going before, and her third last time out offers a sliver of encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Hibernate is the sole confirmed front-runner in an eight-runner field over 1m4f on Good ground at Ffos Las, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, he is set to dictate an uncontested, sustainable gallop from the front. Behind him, Robusto and King's Castle are the most natural prominent horses and will look to slot in close to the pace, while Raintown, Crackergee, Flightofthephoenix, Luan, and Shaffron are all hold-up or midfield types in varying degrees. This field contains more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate naturally — Flightofthephoenix, Luan, and Shaffron are true closers redistributed into the midfield on the map, and in practice they may find themselves further back than ideal with little cover to race against. The uncontested, controlled pace Hibernate sets on Good ground over this stiff 1m4f trip strongly favours horses racing close to him in a prominent or tracking position — those with natural hold-up profiles will face an attritional gallop that does not sharpen up until late, making it harder to reel in a comfortable leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hibernate Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Hibernate leads at his own tempo with no pressure applied and the field settles conservatively behind him.
scenarios.body: Hibernate dictates an even, unhurried gallop and uses his stamina on the stiff Ffos Las track to grind rivals into submission from the front; Robusto and King's Castle, tracking closely in prominent positions, are best placed to challenge in the straight but may lack the finishing gear to dislodge a confident leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If King's Castle or Robusto push the pace and Hibernate is unable to quicken when challenged in the straight.
scenarios.body: The tempo rises slightly as prominent types press Hibernate through the final quarter-mile, and one of the tracking pair produces enough late momentum to collar him close home on the Good ground; King's Castle's excellent course form (9/15 at similar going, 4 wins) makes him the most dangerous of this group.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and create a true end-to-end gallop that burns off the prominently placed horses.
scenarios.body: Raintown, the most progressive of the hold-up types with strong Good-ground form and the tongue-tie switch, would be the most credible closer given recent winning form over shorter trips suggesting strong reserves; Crackergee's sole win came on Soft over 12f which is a different shape, and the redistributed Flightofthephoenix, Luan, and Shaffron carry style-fit penalties that lower their probability in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches and a slow-burn pace creates a sprint finish that gives the true hold-up horses a genuine run.
scenarios.body: Flightofthephoenix and Shaffron are the most talented of the back-markers on raw form but both carry redistribution and style-fit flags, meaning they are unlikely to get their ideal position or rhythm in this race shape; the scenario is low probability precisely because the pace map does not generate the fast-pace conditions these horses need to close.

watchPoints.text: King's Castle has nine runs at similar going with four wins and eight places — if he slots just behind Hibernate and travels smoothly, his course-specific record makes him the most dangerous horse in the race.

Hibernate's uncontested lead is the critical variable: if Robusto or King's Castle push him harder than expected into the final turn, his ability to find extra late on the Good ground — having raced mostly over shorter trips — is genuinely untested.

Raintown arrives fresh off a 14-day break with the tongue-tie applied and two recent wins on Good ground — his handicapper-friendly mark and recency could see him mount a late challenge if Hibernate's lead softens the field up.

Flightofthephoenix, Luan, and Shaffron are all true hold-up types mapped forward on the race shape — watch how they jump and whether they genuinely hold their shown positions or drift back, as that will determine whether any late-race scenario remains viable.
Crackergee's record at similar going is 0W0P from 13 starts — David Probert's experience is an asset but this horse's pattern suggests the conditions consistently fail to unlock his best form.
